text.p: SME - The Central Referendum Committee is expected to declare referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential election invalid since they were carried out with ballots which were not approved by the committee.
- Jan Carnogursky, leader of the strongest opposition party, the Christian Democrtic Movement (KDH), has called for Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to resign for allegedly thwarting the referendums.
- President Michal Kovac said he considered the referendums as foiled and accused Interior Minister Gustav Krajci and Premier Meciar of hindering the plebiscites.
- The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said it insisted on Slovakia's military neutrality and that it may initiate a new referendum on the question.

- The strongest opposition parties have agreed to call an extraordinary session of parliamnet where they will seek the dismissal of Krajci. The opposition also plans to present a new law on direct presidential elections.
PRAVDA - The opposition and coalition have accused each other of thwarting the referendum on NATO mebership and presidential elections.

NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has decided not to add liquidity to the local money market to prevent speculators from playing on the depreciation of the currency by obtaining crowns.
- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Slovakia was showing positive development in many macroeconomic figures, including inflation, unemployment and GDP growth.
- Slovakia's largest producer of cement Hirocem a.s., controlled by the world's largest cement producer Holderbank, said it expected a construction boom to start in Slovakia in the near future.

- An unspecified Japanese bank is ready to extend a 300 million crown loan to cover part of the restructuring of engineering company Pohronske Strojarne but the company's management have yet to find guarantees for the credit.
- Local forex dealers say the crown has so far not been negatively influenced by downward pressure from foreign speculators.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Minister Krajci said he was considering initiating legal action against mayors who refused to accept and distribute referendum ballots with three questions on NATO membership but without a question on direct presidential elections.
